Simulate responses from a fitted beta interval model

Source: R/simulate-brsmm.R
simulate.brs.Rd

Draws new responses from a brs or brsmm fit at the estimated parameters, coarsened with the cells of the fit, as brs_sim and brsmm_sim do.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'brs'
simulate(object, nsim = 1, seed = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'brsmm'
simulate(object, nsim = 1, seed = NULL, re = c("marginal", "conditional"), ...)

Arguments

object

A fitted "brs" or "brsmm" object.

nsim

Number of simulated response vectors (default 1).

seed

NULL or an integer seed, as in simulate: with a seed the caller's RNG state is restored afterwards.

...

Currently ignored.

re

For brsmm fits: "marginal" (default; new random effects in each simulation) or "conditional" (random effects at the conditional modes).

Value

A data frame with nsim columns sim_1, ..., one row per observation of the fit, and the attribute "seed" (as simulate). For brsmm fits with re = "marginal", the attribute "ranef" holds the random effects of each simulation (a list of matrices, one row per group).

Details

Each simulation draws one latent beta value per row with the fitted shapes and returns its score on \(0, \ldots, K\) (cells of the fit's interval map, or its estimated boundary cutpoints); rows fitted as exact values (\(\delta = 0\)) get the latent value itself.

For a brsmm fit, re = "marginal" (default) draws new random effects \(b_g \sim N(0, \hat D)\) for each simulation (new groups with the same design: the marginal distribution of the data), in the order of brsmm_sim, so simulate(fit, seed = s) and set.seed(s); brsmm_sim(...) with the estimates as true values give the same scores. re = "conditional" keeps the random effects at their conditional modes (ranef.brsmm) and draws only the latent values: the same groups again.

See also

brs_sim, brsmm_sim

Examples

set.seed(2023)
d <- data.frame(x = runif(150))
s <- brs_sim(~ x, data = d, beta = c(-0.5, 1), phi = qlogis(0.3), ncuts = 10)
fit <- brs(y ~ x, data = s)
sims <- simulate(fit, nsim = 200, seed = 1)
# Observed and simulated frequencies of the scores
rbind(observed = tabulate(s$y + 1, 11) / nrow(s),
      simulated = tabulate(unlist(sims) + 1, 11) / (200 * nrow(s)))
#>             [,1]       [,2]      [,3]      [,4]   [,5]      [,6]      [,7]
#> observed  0.0400 0.07333333 0.1066667 0.1266667 0.1200 0.1266667 0.1200000
#> simulated 0.0418 0.09500000 0.1001333 0.1044667 0.1065 0.1078333 0.1032333
#>                 [,8]       [,9]      [,10]      [,11]
#> observed  0.06666667 0.08666667 0.07333333 0.06000000
#> simulated 0.10476667 0.10166667 0.09416667 0.04043333
